author: scikit-image developers (individual per-image authors not recorded in the distributed package)
license: BSD-3-Clause (CODE ONLY - image data licences are per-image and NOT stated in the package)
count_basis: VERIFIED by enumeration: the scikit-image 0.26.0 wheel contains 28 image files under skimage/data/ totalling 5,477,469 bytes.
consent_position: UNCLEAR. astronaut.png depicts an identifiable person (Eileen Collins, NASA); several other images are third-party photographs whose authors are credited only in upstream web documentation.
notes: AWAITING PERMISSION. The scikit-image *code* is BSD-3-Clause, but that licence does not automatically extend to the bundled *data*. The package's own skimage/data/README.txt states only that the directory holds sample data and that the full set can be fetched via download_all(); it records no per-image licence. Per-image licences and credits exist in the upstream web documentation, which is outside this sandbox's egress allowlist and therefore could not be transcribed and verified. Until each image's licence and attribution is recorded individually in this manifest, the source stays awaiting_permission and is NOT collected. This is the gate working as intended: an ambiguous rights position is never resolved by assuming the most permissive reading. ADDITIONAL ACCESS FINDING: pypi.org/robots.txt explicitly disallows '/pypi/*/json', so the pypi_wheel adapter is refused by this pipeline's robots.txt gate for that host and must not be used against PyPI. Obtain the images from the upstream repository or the documented skimage.data.download_all() fetcher instead, once per-image licences are transcribed.

author: Yiting Dong et al. (UnsafeBench project, unsafebench.github.io)

Two provenance axes: real-world vs AI-generated.

citation: Dong et al., UnsafeBench: Benchmarking Image Safety Classifiers on Real-World and AI-Generated Images.
notes: AWAITING PERMISSION - RECOMMENDED PRIMARY SOURCE for the content-safety arm of the project. Legitimately curated, human-annotated, purpose-built for exactly this research question, and released by an academic group under a DUA. Requires the researcher to (a) hold a Hugging Face account, (b) read and accept the DUA, and (c) obtain institutional ethics sign-off. Not reachable from this sandbox (huggingface.co is outside the egress allowlist), and this pipeline will never accept DUA terms on the researcher's behalf. Run scripts/collect.py against this manifest on your own network after your DUA is accepted.

source_name: LSPD - Large-Scale Pornographic Dataset for detection and classification
author: LSPD authors (see publication); distribution is by request to the authors
license: custom research licence, granted by the authors on request ('to ensure fair use')
count_basis: Stated by the authors: 500,000 images and 4,000 videos, of which more than 50,000 images carry annotation (93,810 labelled instances).
label_definitions: Image/video classification: porn, normal, sexy, hentai, drawings.
Instance segmentation: polygon masks for four private sexual object classes (breasts, male genital, female genital, anus).
consent_position: Authors state pornographic images were sourced from adult websites; per-image consent and age-verification records are not conveyed to downstream researchers.
citation: LSPD: A Large-Scale Pornographic Dataset for Detection and Classification (2022).
notes: AWAITING PERMISSION, WITH A CAVEAT YOU SHOULD WEIGH. This is the standard academic benchmark for this task and is cited widely, but its underlying images are themselves scraped from adult websites, so the consent chain that a *direct* scrape lacks is only partly repaired by routing through the authors. If you use it: request access formally, record the authors' written terms in this manifest, keep the data on controlled institutional storage, publish metrics only, and get ethics-board sign-off. Do not mirror it.

author: deepghs
license: MIT (as declared on the dataset card)
count_basis: Card states 10K-100K images organised into five classes following the standard NSFW-detection categorisation. Exact per-class counts must be enumerated after access.
label_definitions: Five classes representing escalating levels of explicitness in artistic/illustrated content, following the popular NSFW-detection implementations.
consent_position: UNCLEAR. A declared MIT licence on the dataset card does not establish that the uploader held rights to the underlying images, and much of this class of corpus is artwork scraped from illustration platforms.
notes: AWAITING PERMISSION. Deliberately NOT auto-approved despite carrying an MIT tag. A permissive licence declared by an anonymous re-uploader is only as good as that uploader's own rights in the images, which cannot be verified from here; the card itself flags the content as Not-For-All-Audiences. Treat a self-declared licence on scraped NSFW imagery as unverified until the provenance chain is documented. If you need illustrated-content moderation, prefer a source whose curators state their collection method.

Research-only intent is stated explicitly, which is the closest any of these come to a usable grant, but the licence is unidentifiable ('other'), the content is uncensored real-person explicit imagery, and no per-image consent chain exists. source_name: C4Censor - lightweight benchmark for inappropriate content detection
author: C4Censor authors (Journal of Information Security and Applications / Springer)
license: not stated in the accessible abstract - must be obtained from the authors or publisher
count_basis: Described as lightweight: 4 coarse classes (Blood & Gore, Pornography, Terrorism, Neutral) subdivided into 12 fine-grained subclasses, manually annotated at both levels.
label_definitions: Coarse (4-way): Blood & Gore, Pornography, Terrorism, Neutral.
Fine (12-way): subclasses such as Hentai vs photographic, per the paper.
consent_position: Authors state all visuals were scraped from publicly accessible sources (YouTube/Twitch gaming streams, medical-procedure archives, specialty NSFW collections, X and Telegram extremist-tracking channels) and manually annotated. Scraped provenance means per-subject consent is not established.
notes: AWAITING PERMISSION. Methodologically attractive because its multi-class fine-grained labels go beyond the usual binary porn-vs-neutral framing, which suits your 'visual content classification' and 'general visual-category recognition' objectives. Licence terms are not published in the accessible record, so contact the authors.

author: EBazarov; alex000kim
license: repository licence covers the URL lists only, NOT the images they point at
count_basis: Stated: 1,589,331 NSFW image URLs across 159 categories; the companion neutral list holds 36,837 URLs. These are LINKS, not images.
label_definitions: Category label per URL, derived from the originating subreddit/channel.
consent_position: NONE. The target URLs point at third-party hosts (Reddit CDNs, image hosts, adult sites). Resolving them means scraping third-party websites and extracting embedded media without authorisation from the hosts or the depicted subjects.
notes: REJECTED - do not use this route even though the URL lists themselves are open. This is the mechanism by which a great deal of NSFW research data has been built, and it is precisely what your own protocol forbids: 'Do not scrape third-party websites or extract embedded media without authorization.' The repository is explicitly marked historical and no longer maintained, so a large fraction of URLs are dead, and the remainder resolve to hosts whose robots.txt and terms forbid automated collection. The age-verification and consent position of the destinations is unverifiable at corpus scale. Use a curated, DUA-gated corpus (UnsafeBench, USD) instead.
